title: Per-variant memory fingerprinting and allocator hints for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal:
Create model-specific memory fingerprints and allocator hint layers for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants configured for long-context (16k+). Use these fingerprints to: (1) reduce peak GPU memory by 6-20% for typical chat/streaming workloads, (2) bound tail latencies under continuous batching, and (3) enable deterministic eviction decisions for KV cache slices across mixed-variant fleets.

Background:
We observe high variance in KV residency patterns and peak allocator pressure across model variants and quantization paths. Existing generic memory profiles over-allocate for some variants (Mistral-extended) and under-optimize for others (Qwen-32k int8 cross-attention). This ticket implements a reproducible pipeline that: extracts per-variant per-seqlen memory fingerprints, synthesizes allocator hints (preferred slab sizes, eager/ lazy compaction thresholds, KV slice alignment), and ships runtime flags + verification tests.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 95th-percentile peak GPU resident memory reduced by >=6% on benchmark traces for each target variant at target long contexts (8k, 16k, 32k) compared to baseline profile.
- End-to-end P99 token latency degradation under continuous batching <=+8% while maintaining throughput parity.
- KV cache eviction-induced generation inconsistencies (token divergence) remain <=0.5% on our eval prompt set.
- Automated profile generator produces a candidate artifact for each variant that passes CI memory/regression checks.

Approach / Workplan:
1) Data collection (week 1-2): run per-layer memory instrumentation across representative traces (conversations, single long prompts, high-terminate-rate generation). Capture: per-token allocator growth, KV residency heatmaps, peak stack+heap+device allocations.
2) Fingerprint synthesis (week 2): aggregate traces to produce deterministic fingerprints composed of: per-layer peak, typical working-set window, kv-slice-occupancy histogram, and per-batch growth slope.
3) Allocator hint generator (week 2-3): map fingerprints to allocator parameters: slab bucket targets, slab split thresholds, KV slice alignment granularity (32/64/128 KB), and preferred prefetching hints for attention keys/values.
4) Runtime integration (week 3): add flagged runtime path that consumes profile JSON and applies hints at model load + during hot-swap. Ensure flags are reversible and default to existing profile when no match.
5) CI & verification (week 3-4): stress tests, memory regression tests, and token-consistency evals.
6) Docs & rollout (week 4): PRD addendum, rollout plan for Dedicated fleets and hosted fallback policies.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Overfitting: profiles tuned on synthetic traces may regress on real customer inputs. Mitigation: include held-out traces from production anonymized set and compare token-consistency.
- Runtime complexity: more profiles increases matching overhead. Mitigation: implement a lightweight fingerprint matcher (bloom-filter style signature) and fall back to default.
- Quantization interactions: int8 execution paths change per-layer memory layout; profiles must be quant-aware. We'll tag fingerprints with quantization metadata.

Deliverables:
- profile artifacts: runtime-profile-llama-16k.json, runtime-profile-mistral-32k-q8.json, runtime-profile-qwen-64k-q4.json (stored in s3://redwood-runtime-profiles/)
- allocator-hints library with tests
- runtime flag and loader implementation + integration tests
- performance dashboard: Grafana panels for peak resident memory and KV residency per variant

Acceptance criteria checklist:
- [ ] fingerprint generator commit merged
- [ ] 3 variant profiles generated and validated against held-out traces
- [ ] runtime loader and unit tests merged
- [ ] CI memory/regression gates pass on runtime-1.21 branch
- [ ] performance dashboard shows improvements and is linked in the PR
